Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis are trading increasingly intense strikes on strategic sites, including oil infrastructure and ports, marking a sharp escalation in fighting between the two sides.
A projectile struck an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia’s southwestern Jazan region on Thursday, killing a Nepalese worker and injuring several others, according to the Saudi Ministry of Energy. The strike sparked a fire and temporarily suspended some operations at the facility, the ministry said.
The attack came a day after the Houthis claimed to have struck Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil refinery at Ras Tanura. Satellite imagery taken Wednesday showed a huge plume of black smoke rising from the coastal peninsula following the attack.

Two Italian nationals were killed on Thursday in an Iranian drone attack on the Gulf nation of Kuwait, Italy’s Foreign Minister said. Tehran denied any involvement in the incident.
Antonio Tajani said “several drones of Iranian origin targeted Kuwaiti military installations” including an “air defence detection station where two Italian technicians from (Rome-based defense company) Rheinmetall Italia were working.”
“A powerful explosion occurred, and, according to reports reaching us from Kuwait, both of our fellow citizens have unfortunately died,” Tajani said in a statement.

item.title: Netanyahu gets major legal boost as court casts doubt on corruption case
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s yearslong corruption trial took a significant turn in his favor on Wednesday as judges recommended that prosecutors drop charges in the most serious of the three cases against him and reconsider a second case.

item.title: Young Britons’ sex lives have fallen off a cliff, major survey shows
item.description: Young Britons are having half as much sex as they were in 1990, according to a new study, with the average reported frequency falling from four times a month to just twice a month.
